text:
I spent the weekend testing local text embeddings directly on an Android device to make debug logs searchable using natural language.

Normally, searching through thousands of lines of client-side logs during QA requires exact keyword matches or exporting everything to an external tool. I wanted to see if a small 22M parameter model running via ONNX Runtime Mobile could generate vector embeddings fast enough on a midrange phone.

The results surprised me. Generating embeddings for 500 log entries took under 120 milliseconds on CPU, with zero noticeable impact on main thread rendering. Storing those vectors in a local database allowed me to query terms like "checkout network timeout" and instantly surface the relevant stack trace.

Processing logs locally keeps sensitive data on-device, eliminates API calls, and gives developers a powerful diagnostic tool inside debug builds.

Have you experimented with running lightweight vector models locally inside your mobile apps yet?
